events.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

message.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

args.content:
# Reading list

A small Next.js app for tracking what you're reading. No accounts, no database —
books are stored in `data/books.json`, so they survive a restart.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3000
npm test         # store + form action tests
```

- `/` — currently reading, finished, and the form for adding a book
- `/books/<id>` — one book's title, author and notes; this is the link to share

Book ids come from the title (`/books/piranesi`) so shared links stay readable.
Set `BOOKS_DATA_DIR` to keep the JSON file somewhere other than `./data`.

`npm run build && npm start` for the production server.

events.content:
Built and verified. `npm run dev` → http://localhost:3000.

**What's there**

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `lib/books.js` | JSON-file store — read, add, set status, update notes |
| `app/page.jsx` | Currently reading / Finished lists + add form |
| `app/books/[id]/page.jsx` | One book: title, author, notes — the shareable link |
| `app/actions.js` | Server actions the forms post to |
| `components/AddBookForm.jsx`, `NotesForm.jsx` | The two interactive forms |

**Decisions worth knowing about**

- **Ids come from the title**, so a shared link reads `/books/piranesi` rather than a UUID. Duplicate titles get a short random suffix. Non-latin-only titles fall back to `book`.
- **Writes go through a promise chain.** Two form submits landing at once would otherwise each save a copy of the list missing the other's book. Writes are also write-then-rename, so a crash can't truncate the file.
- **Notes are editable on the book page** — "see my notes" implies somewhere to put them, and notes accrue while you read.
- **Finished is reversible** (a "Move back to reading" button on the book page) so a misclick isn't permanent. Same code path as marking finished.
- **`data/books.json` is gitignored** — your reading list isn't source code. It's created on first add.

**Verification** — 17 tests pass (`npm test`), production build clean, and I drove the running server: added books, marked one finished over the real form POST (moved sections, dated correctly), loaded both detail pages, got a 404 page for an unknown id, then restarted the server and confirmed the books were still there.

Two things I checked rather than assumed:

- `Æther` slugged to `ther-...` — NFKD leaves Æ/Ø intact, so the accent-stripping regex dropped them mid-word. Added a transliteration pass; it's `aether` now.
- While probing actions over HTTP I hit a 500 from `addBookAction` when `formData` was absent. That was my hand-rolled request missing the state field React sends, not a path a browser takes — the real form works. I left the action as-is rather than adding a guard for a request only I made.

I deleted the sample books (Dune, Piranesi) I used for testing, so you'll open to an empty list.
